title: Hackers reportedly breached CIA intelligence analysis system
content_md: ​Unknown attackers have reportedly breached an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), according to a source familiar with the matter. The source told The New York Times , which first reported the incident, that the cyberattack was carried out using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework and also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. While the CIA and the ODNI have not yet replied to a request for more details regarding this incident, no classified data or systems were exposed in the breach. "The hack did not involve our classified networks or classified information, and no other systems are currently at risk," the source said. Hours after the CIA security breach was reported, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) also disclosed that it's investigating a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. After detecting the attack, the agency took some systems offline as a precaution and told banks to use the Financial Institutions Hotline to file reports, since some services may be unavailable. FinCEN is a US Department of the Treasury bureau that acts as the country's official Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and protects the nation's financial system from illicit activities by sharing financial intelligence with law enforcement agencies both domestically and internationally.
